name: Samak Pulao
steps: Pick over the barnyard millet, rinse in a fine sieve and soak in fresh water for 15 minutes. Drain completely; this soaking water is separate from the measured cooking water.
Peel the potato and cut into 1 cm cubes. Finely chop the chilli and coriander. Measure the cooking water before starting so the small grains do not sit in the hot pan too long.
Warm the ghee in a heavy saucepan. Fry the peanuts over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes until lightly golden, then lift them out. Add cumin to the remaining ghee and let it sizzle.
Add potato and chilli and cook for 3 minutes, turning often. Stir in the drained millet for 30 seconds, then add the measured water and rock salt. Bring to a gentle boil.

Cover and cook over low heat for 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed, the potato is tender and the millet is soft. If the grains remain firm, add a small splash of hot water and cook covered for 2 minutes more.
Remove from the heat and rest covered for 5 minutes. Fold in the fried peanuts, lemon juice and coriander gently with a fork; avoid vigorous stirring, which makes the millet pasty.
tips: Samak is barnyard millet, not ordinary rice. This potato-and-peanut version is not automatically suitable for a Jain household.
passiveTime: Soak millet for 15 minutes; rest the cooked pulao for 5 minutes.
notes: Four adult portions. Listed time covers preparation and cooking; additional soaking, cooling or resting is stated separately. Fasting customs vary: check every ingredient against your household practice. Jain suitability depends on your saved ingredient rules.
